title: The two sides offer different countries as places a consignment can travel through: DR1 lists 41, including French Guiana, Réunion, Mayotte and the Channel Islands but not Norway or Switzerland; the frontend lists 31, the EU 27 plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

finding.frontend: The checkboxes are drawn from the frontend's origin-country list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:22-27). Thirty-one entries: the twenty-seven EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. No overseas territory or Crown Dependency appears, and no country outside the EU and EFTA does either. Three labels differ from DR1's for the same place — "Czechia", "Ireland" and "Netherlands (the)".
finding.prototype: The search is fed a forty-one entry list (app/views/transit-countries.html:75). It holds the twenty-seven EU member states, eleven EU outermost regions and overseas entities — Azores, Canary Islands, Ceuta, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Madeira, Martinique, Mayotte, Melilla, Réunion, Saint Martin — and three Crown Dependencies, Guernsey, Isle of Man and Jersey. Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland are absent. The United Kingdom is absent too, matching the page's own line "This does not include the United Kingdom".
finding.difference: Settle which list is right before changing either side, because taking DR1 literally would both add and remove countries and each direction looks wrong on its face. DR1's own copy defines these as "countries between the country of origin and the destination country" — a consignment does not travel through Réunion, Mayotte, Martinique or French Guiana on its way to Great Britain, so DR1's data contradicts DR1's sentence; and dropping Switzerland and Norway would stop a user recording the most ordinary road route into GB from southern Europe. What settles it is the authoritative list of countries a consignment may be recorded as transiting — the same list the backend validates the submitted notification against — and a decision on whether one shared country list can serve both "where is this party's address" and "where does the consignment pass through", which is what put the territories in DR1's transit list in the first place. On the frontend the two questions already share one list too, so the change is not local to this page.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding Norway, Switzerland, Iceland or Liechtenstein in DR1's transit-country data, or finding any of the eleven overseas territories in the frontend's — the two datasets are captured in full in the rendered DOM for each screen and neither overlaps the other on those entries.
finding.verification: Listed both datasets out of the captured DOM, not the page model, and counted them by hand. The frontend's checkbox group holds exactly 31 labels, Austria to Switzerland, which are the 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland — no territory, no dependency, nothing outside the EU and EFTA. DR1's app-transit-country-search__data holds exactly 41 entries: the same 27 member states, the 11 outermost regions and overseas entities the finding names, and Guernsey, Isle of Man and Jersey. Ran the falsifier both ways: Norway, Switzerland, Iceland and Liechtenstein are absent from DR1's list, and none of the 11 territories appears in the frontend's, so it does not fire. The three differing labels are exact — DR1 says "Czech Republic", "Republic of Ireland" and "Netherlands" where the frontend says "Czechia", "Ireland" and "Netherlands (the)". Read DR1's transit-countries.html whole and confirmed the intro copy the difference slot quotes, at :46-47. Rubric 7 fires and the disputed band is right; the contradiction is flatter than the finding argues. Recorded in correction; the slots are left as written.
finding.correction:
No claim fell; two notes, both in the finding's favour. Understated: the finding rests the DR1 self-contradiction on inference — that a consignment does not travel through Réunion or French Guiana on its way to Great Britain. DR1 contradicts itself more plainly than that. Its page carries the line "This does not include the United Kingdom" at transit-countries.html:47, and three of the 41 entries it offers are labelled "Guernsey (United Kingdom)", "Isle of Man (United Kingdom)" and "Jersey (United Kingdom)", each carrying "parent":"United Kingdom" in DR1's own data. Checked by reading the countriesJson payload out of the captured DOM against the view source. That is the observation that makes the list genuinely undecidable rather than merely awkward, and it is why the band stands. Second, a quoting slip that changes nothing: DR1's data spells the entry "Reunion (France)", without the accent the title and the difference slot give it.

DUPLICATE SWEEP: both findings survive. origin-and-reason--country-list-omits-territories describes the same two lists in different words — the same DR1 41, the same frontend 31, the same three naming differences — and neither finding knew of the other. This one already says the frontend's two questions share a list; they share it with a third. Checked rather than inferred: `countries.originCountries()` has exactly three callers in the whole app, origin/controller.js:60, destination-country/controller.js:27 and this page's transit-countries.controller.js:23, all fed from one GBNAG_SPS_EX block at services/countries/index.js:24. That makes the ruling this finding asks for wider than it states: it is not only whether one list can serve "where is this party's address" and "where does the consignment pass through", but that the other finding treats removing Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland as settled work while this one holds that removing Norway and Switzerland breaks the ordinary road route into GB. The two are not merged — they sit either side of a band boundary, `disputed` against `needs-backend`, and the questions may legitimately want different lists — but they cannot be actioned independently.

relatedTo.why: One list, not two. That finding describes the same 41-against-31 difference on the origin and destination questions, which read the same countries.originCountries() this page reads, and asks for the EFTA removal this finding disputes.
